footnotes:
Langwill 1980: 93 mentions one “descant trombone” in Burgdorf. Bachmann-Geiser 1998 mentions only a
“Diskant-Posaune” in Burgdorf, Inv. 1098. Leutenegger 1956 refers to instrument as a Diskantposaune Beat Gugger
(letter to the author of 25 May 1999) affirms there are two, both dated 1697.
location: CH-BU, RS XIII 1099; ex Jegenstorf Church.
signature: : “MACHT IOHANN CARL KODISCH NURNBERG 1697”; master’s mark, “I C K” with prancing horse.
dimensions: H 110, be 125. My meas.: mp receiver 11.7, slide sec. 1605.5, overlap impossible to measure; bell sec. 1017.5 (not including portion overlapped in slide sec.); total le 2623.
remarks: ****Beat Gugger, Museumsleiter of the Burgdorf Schlossmuseum (letter to the author, 25 May 1999) affirms there are two, both dated 1697. Letter from Gugger: “Bestimmung: E. Leutenegger, Burgdorf / Revidiert durch N. Spada, Burgdorf, am 3.März 1954.” Slide has been reversed; patch at bottom of desc. Slide tube, ca. 65mm from end; bell sec. essentially identical to 16971; pin in bell stay is same as 1697-1, but mounted upside down; repair in bell sec.—large patch 40 mm from bell opening; impossible to separate slide and bell sec. Examined by the author June 1999. My notes say slide frozen, bore not measureable.
